problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & -1 & 8 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix
examples.problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd and $4$th rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/a29e80b35c9505ee665a109978de9b936ee7ce59eef631d7af9a4b7954bd8696.png)
examples.worked_solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1$st, $3$rd and $4$th rows of $A$ are $-1$, $-4$ and $8$, respectively.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14071571/assets/d2f89fe83787daf667e01fd4c4fe644bc36cfe23b046088c22e8de17bb02dc28.png)

So, the answer is $-1+(-4)+8=3.$
